reasons: Strongest attack on A: dispatch and shared options must be hand-written (add_subparsers + set_defaults(func=...)); without required=True a bare run raises AttributeError; parse_args exits via SystemExit so tests must catch it; no CliRunner equivalent.
Not decisive: these are 20-30 lines of one-time boilerplate, avoidable with required=True, dest and main(argv).
B and C add a permanent dependency to a repo with no manifest; C (typer) is the most fragile (0.x, pulls click, rich, shellingham).

evidence.claim: No dependency manifest in the repo; only .free-hands/ is tracked.

risks: Unverified recollections about click 8.2 / typer version pinning.
Switch to B if the tool is planned to grow into nested groups/completion or the repo/org standardizes on click.
would_change_if: The repo already declares click/typer, or the tool is planned to exceed three simple subcommands.
